title: NASA Selects Astranis for NEXUS Ka-Band Relay Satellite Program
body_markdown:
**SAN FRANCISCO, November 5, 2026.** Today Astranis announced it has been selected by NASA for the initial phase of its[Network Extension for User Continuity and Sustainability (NEXUS) project](https://www.nasa.gov/general/nextstep-3-e-network-extension-for-user-continuity-and-sustainability-nexus-ka-band-backward-compatible-relay-broad/) , developing a Ka-band relay capability to support legacy relay users, so existing missions can continue to operate as the Tracking and Data Relay Satellite (TDRS) fleet in geosynchronous orbit (GSO) is retired. Astranis’ contract has a maximum potential value of $264.3 million and supports NASA’s adoption of a commercial services model instead of a government-owned system.


Project NEXUS supports NASA’s decision to gradually retire its TDRS fleet and adopt commercial services for future missions. Legacy TDRS users cannot practically alter their communications hardware or switch to incompatible commercial services, and require backward-compatible Ka-band relay support to stay connected.


“Keeping NASA’s most important missions connected takes infrastructure that is resilient, proven, and built to last,” said John Gedmark, CEO and cofounder of Astranis. “NEXUS puts our production capacity to work for NASA, using the same dual-use spacecraft platforms designed to serve our commercial customers.”


Under the firm-fixed-price contract, NASA is funding initial concept development and risk reduction. The period of performance for the initial phase runs Nov 4, 2026 through May 3, 2027, with follow-on phases extending the work through 2029. The NEXUS acquisition is structured as a complete service, including space and ground systems, launch and deployment, on-orbit demonstration, and a future operational service phase. NASA's objective for NEXUS is to acquire backward-compatible Ka-band relay services capable of supporting existing missions for at least 15 years.


NEXUS is facilitated through the Communications Services Project within NASA’s Space Communications and Navigation (SCaN) division, through which[Astranis](https://www.astranis.com/) is partnered with NASA on a nonreimbursable Space Act Agreement.


**About Astranis**


Astranis builds[advanced satellites for high orbits](https://www.astranis.com/spacecraft) , expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly sophisticated customers across the globe - large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military.


With multiple satellites now on orbit serving customers around the world, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.


Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, BlackRock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.
